baseline.name: Rebuild filtered digits for every query
baseline.approach: Scan each substring, append its nonzero digits modulo MOD and sum its digits.
baseline.time: O(sum of query widths), at most O(q*m)
baseline.space: O(1) working arithmetic state plus output

archived.name: Prefix sums, retained-digit prefixes and powers
archived.space: O(m) four auxiliary arrays plus O(q) output

why: Prefix differences recover digit sums and retained-digit counts, while modular prefix removal recovers each filtered number without rescanning the substring.
quantitative_comparison: The baseline revisits every queried character. The archive performs one m-character preprocessing pass and a bounded number of arithmetic/array operations per query; benefit depends on total query width exceeding setup work. No measured speedup is asserted.
tradeoffs: Preprocessing can be unnecessary for one short query and uses several full-length arrays. Partial allocation failure leaks successful allocations; index/arithmetic assumptions remain. Source kernel/stack comments are not validated performance evidence.
evidence_basis: Static preprocessing-versus-rescan work model with exact allocation trade-offs; no matched benchmark.
